source_excerpts.text:
# A local criterion for reference-uniform channel order

## 1. Inputs and consequence

Let P and Q be finite classical channels on the same n-letter input. We use output-by-input matrices: entries are nonnegative and every column sums to one. Remove identically zero output rows. Assume every remaining output row of BOTH channels has at most two positive entries. The input alphabet, output counts, support graph, and number of overlapping cycles are unrestricted.

For an unordered pair e={i,j}, oriented by i<j, an output row supported exactly on e has coefficients (a,b)>0. Define

    k_e(t) = sum_(Q rows on e) ab/(a+bt)
             - sum_(P rows on e) ab/(a+bt),      t>0.                 (1)

An empty sum is zero. Singleton rows do not enter (1).

**Theorem 1.** The following statements are equivalent:

1. Every k_e is nonnegative on (0,infinity).
2. For every finite real or complex Hilbert space, every positive definite selfadjoint operator A_i on that space, and every vector x_i,

       sum_y <sum_i P_yi x_i, (sum_i P_yi A_i)^-1 sum_i P_yi x_i>
       >= the corresponding sum for Q.                              (2)

3. P dominates Q in ordinary classical less-noisy / relative-entropy order.
4. P dominates Q in complete SLD order, allowing every finite untouched quantum reference, every faithful baseline, and every traceless Hermitian tangent.
5. P dominates Q in unrestricted complete Umegaki relative-entropy order: all finite references and all input-state pairs, with NO equal-reference-marginal restriction.

In fact (1) also implies comparison of every operator-convex Petz f-divergence and the associated resolvent quadratic forms after every finite reference. No stochastic postprocessing map is asserted.

The equivalence of 4 and 5 for arbitrary channels is an accepted programme input, N675 Theorem 1.2(2), source lines101–125 and172 onward. We prove the structured reduction, including the stronger operator statement (2), rather than re-auditing N675. The source snapshot is pinned at ad7ff1b9d15a774d4b4d8362314c7070cac030e5 / input5788b347..., subsequently historical after a later refresh failed. The packet's explicit human programme-acceptance notice governs its older source-history labels.

This theorem supplies an exact finite operation on a class with unbounded input dimension and outcome counts. It does not provide a reference cutoff or an algorithm

# From exact support to an open coherent design region

This develops Theorem1 beyond a sparse comparison compiler. Its conclusion concerns a FULL open neighbourhood of quantum POVM pairs: the perturbed effects need not be positive mixtures of a common primitive or retain pair-supported coefficient rows. All untouched reference dimensions are covered by one quantitative coercivity argument.

## 1. General input contract

Let M_1,...,M_n be a strictly positive, linearly independent informationally complete POVM on C^d, with n=d^2. Supply rational bounds

    m I <= M_i <= M I,          0<m<=M.

Let P,Q be the pair-supported channels of the main theorem and E=P M, F=Q M. Suppose a connected graph G on the n primitive outcomes and delta>0 satisfy

    k_ij(t) >= delta/(1+t)  for every edge of G and every t>0.         (1)

Other pair kernels may be nonnegative and can be discarded in a lower bound. Supply a rational graph bound lambda>0 with

    L_G >= lambda (I-11^T/n).                                       (2)

Let r_y=sum_i P_yi (and similarly for Q); every output row is nonzero. Write m_y=m r_y. Take eta>0 with eta<=1 and eta<=min_y m_y/2. Let c be any rational upper bound on sqrt(n), and define

    K = sum_(all P and Q rows y)
         [4c/m + 2n/(m r_y) + 2/m^2],
    alpha = delta*m*lambda/(2M^2).                                  (3)

The conclusions below hold whenever K eta < alpha. These conservative constants are not claimed sharp.

## 2. Remove the reference gauge before perturbing

For a faithful baseline on A R and any Hermitian tangent, let S_i and X_i be the primitive reference blocks. Their sums are S=rho_R>0 and X=H_R. Put Lambda=J_S and L=Lambda^-1 X. Replace X_i by

    X_i^0 = X_i-J_{S_i}L,             sum_i X_i^0=0.                  (4)

Every trace-preserving measurement channel has the same reference marginal. Its SLD quadratic form therefore equals its quadratic form on the adjusted tangent plus <X,Lambda^-1 X>. To see this, expand each output inverse quadratic after subtracting J_(output baseline)L. The cross terms sum to 2 Tr[(sum output X^0)L]=0, and the gauge squares sum to <L,Lambda L>. Consequently the E-minus-F gap is UNCHANGED by (4). The same holds for every perturbed POVM below. No equal-reference restriction has been inserted into the original order; (4) is an exact gauge identity.

Whiten Lambda and set

    B_i=Lambda^-1/2

# A dimension-uniform information-thinning construction

The localizer is not limited to certifying exactly pair-supported output arrays or a tiny perturbation of one qubit example. A connected well-conditioned primitive yields a strict RELATIVE conditional-information gap. Constant-degree expanders turn that into a fixed global-erasure budget with only linearly many classical readout outcomes. The resulting erasure row has full input support and is outside the pair-output compiler.

## 1. General theorem: graph gap becomes a global-erasure budget

Use the notation and hypotheses of COHERENT_NEIGHBOURHOOD Sections1–3, but informational completeness and linear independence are not needed for the following inequality. Let

    V=sum_i <l_i,B_i l_i>=g_M(H)-g_ref(H_R).

The equality is the reference-gauge decomposition. The weighted-mean argument there gives V<=M sum_i||l_i-lbar||^2. Therefore, BEFORE converting to the Euclidean norm S0,

    g_E-g_F >= gamma (g_M-g_ref),
    gamma=delta*m*lambda_2(L_G)/(2M).                              (1)

Classical postprocessing cannot increase SLD, so

    0<=g_E-g_ref<=g_M-g_ref.

Let Er_gamma(E) be the measurement with effects ((1-gamma)E_y)_y and one additional effect gamma I. For 0<=gamma<=1 its complete SLD form is (1-gamma)g_E+gamma g_ref. Thus (1) implies

    Er_gamma(E) >=_complete SLD F,
    Er_gamma(E) >=_complete unrestricted Umegaki F.                 (2)

The latter step uses accepted N675. Equivalently, for finite divergence values and arbitrary states alpha,beta on A R,

    D(F_R alpha||F_R beta)-D(alpha_R||beta_R)
       <=(1-gamma)[D(E_R alpha||E_R beta)-D(alpha_R||beta_R)].        (3)

The unsubtracted flagged inequality (2) is the governing statement at support boundaries; infinity-minus-infinity is not defined. Setting beta=alpha_R tensor alpha_A gives the fully quantum mutual-information comparison

    I(R:F) <= (1-gamma) I(R:E),       for EVERY state on A R.        (4)

This has the form of a complete RELATIVE contraction coefficient in Belzig–Gao–Smith–Wu Definition7.1, not a contraction of D(E_R alpha||E_R beta) by a number below1 when reference marginals differ. Reference-only information is preserved and must be subtracted or flagged as in (2)–(3).
